rationale: B wins because it turns the ugliest fact into an actual story, not just a pre-flight risk. "Toast's restaurant advances don't disclose default rates. That's the number that matters." is a cleaner reporter hook than A burying the same issue under "Why are default rates on Toast Capital advances undisclosed?" in the uncomfortable-questions section. A is more disciplined in places, but B gives the founder sharper press material, assuming someone scrubs the overclaimed lock-in language before pitching.
gaps_in_A: "Toast got profitable by selling money, not hardware" overstates causality. The update says Toast reached profitability and says fintech is higher-margin; it does not prove fintech caused profitability.

A treats the best skeptical story as homework: "Why are default rates on Toast Capital advances undisclosed?" That should have been a kept lending/data angle, not just a question after the pitch list.

"The fee complaints are a standing vulnerability, not a live news signal" is too dismissive. Bundling lending and payroll onto a platform that some owners already criticize for fees is a legitimate operator-power angle.

"tip pooling, wage credits, variable shifts" may be true restaurant-payroll context, but the update only says tipped and hourly staff. Good instinct, but it needs to be framed as proof to gather, not assumed texture.
gaps_in_B: "opting out of its financial products comes with real friction" is not in the update. POS switching costs may be real, but B states the dependency before proving it.

"a large-scale, publicly traded lender with no disclosed credit performance metrics" overstates the credit scale. Toast is large and public; the update does not give Toast Capital advance volume or loan-book size.

"tipped minimum wage variation by state, tip pooling rules, tip credits, and the mix of hourly and tip-eligible workers" imports specifics the update does not supply. Useful proof targets, sloppy as asserted setup.

"whether Toast's data advantage (it processes the sales that tips derive from) actually produces a differentiated payroll product" decorates the payroll angle with an unproven product claim. The update says Toast processes restaurant sales, not that payroll uses that data.
